## 1. Set up

Run this one time in your R console if needed:

```r
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "httr2", "jsonlite"))
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(httr2)
library(jsonlite)

`%||%` <- function(x, default) if (is.null(x)) default else x

# PILOT ONLY: these are examples, not a representative sample.

# to replace with the finalized game list later
game_ids <- c(1091500, 1172470, 1245620, 1086940)
```

## 2. Collect game information from Steam

`appid` is the unique Steam game ID. We collect the game's name, release date,
price, genre and free-to-play status.

```{r}
get_game <- function(id) {
  raw <- request("https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails") |>
    req_url_query(appids = id, cc = "us", l = "english") |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_json(simplifyVector = FALSE)

  result <- raw[[as.character(id)]]
  if (!isTRUE(result$success)) return(NULL)
  g <- result$data

  # Genres are a list, so combine them into one text field.
  genre_names <- map_chr(g$genres %||% list(),
                         ~ .x$description %||% "")

  tibble(
    appid = id,
    name = g$name %||% NA_character_,
    release_date = g$release_date$date %||% NA_character_,
    genres = paste(genre_names, collapse = ", "),
    free_to_play = g$is_free %||% NA,
    price_usd = if (isTRUE(g$is_free)) 0 else
      (g$price_overview$final %||% NA_real_) / 100
  )
}

# A short pause avoids sending many requests all at once.
games <- map_dfr(game_ids, function(id) {
  Sys.sleep(1)
  get_game(id)
})

glimpse(games)
write_csv(games, "steam_games.csv")


```

## 3. Collect a small sample of recent reviews

This uses Steam's **current GetAppReviews service**, not the older, deprecated
`/appreviews` endpoint. One request returns up to 100 reviews per game.
For now, collect only English-language reviews and do not store reviewer IDs.

```{r}
get_reviews <- function(id) {
  options <- list(
    appid = as.integer(id),
    filter = 1L,             # 1 = most recently created
    review_type = 0L,        # 0 = positive AND negative
    purchase_type = 1L,      # 1 = all purchase sources
    languages = list("english"),
    num_per_page = 100L
  )

  raw <- request("https://api.steampowered.com/IUserReviewsService/GetAppReviews/v1/") |>
    req_url_query(input_json = as.character(toJSON(options, auto_unbox = TRUE))) |>
    req_perform() |>
    resp_body_json(simplifyVector = FALSE)

  # Steam's Web API may return a "response" wrapper.
  data <- raw$response %||% raw
  items <- data$reviews %||% list()
  if (length(items) == 0) return(tibble())

  map_dfr(items, function(r) {
    tibble(
      appid = id,
      review_date = as.Date(as.POSIXct(
        as.numeric(r$timestamp_created %||% NA_real_),
        origin = "1970-01-01", tz = "UTC"
      )),
      positive = r$voted_up %||% NA,
      playtime_hours = (r$author$playtime_at_review %||% NA_real_) / 60,
      review_text = r$review %||% NA_character_
    )
  })
}

reviews <- map_dfr(game_ids, function(id) {
  Sys.sleep(1)
  get_reviews(id)
})

glimpse(reviews)
write_csv(reviews, "steam_reviews_sample.csv")


```

## 4. First EDA

**Data quality:** how many observations and missing values?

```{r}
cat("Games:", nrow(games), "\n")
cat("Reviews:", nrow(reviews), "\n")

reviews |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.x))))
```

**Question 1:** What percent of our *sampled recent reviews* is positive for each game?

```{r}
review_summary <- reviews |>
  group_by(appid) |>
  summarise(
    n_sampled = n(),
    positive_pct = 100 * mean(positive, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  left_join(games |> select(appid, name), by = "appid")

review_summary

ggplot(review_summary, aes(x = reorder(name, positive_pct), y = positive_pct)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Positive Reviews in Our Recent Sample",
       x = "Game", y = "Positive reviews (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

**Question 2:** How many hours had reviewers played when they posted their review?

```{r}
reviews |>
  filter(!is.na(playtime_hours), playtime_hours > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = playtime_hours)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(title = "Playtime at Review (Log Scale)",
       x = "Hours played at time of review", y = "Reviews") +
  theme_minimal()
```

## 5. Limitations and next steps

- These four games are a convenience pilot, not a final unbiased sample.
- Reviews are the most recent ~100 English reviews per game, not all-time review
  sentiment or a random sample. Do not treat the sampled percentage as lifetime
  positive-review percentage.
- `price_usd` is the current US store price, not the launch price.
- Historical monthly concurrent-player data is not included yet. Once we add
  SteamCharts (or another historical source), we can examine how player counts
  change over the first 12–24 months after release.
- Respect Steam's rate limits. If you receive an HTTP 429 or access error,
  stop and try again later rather than repeatedly retrying.
- Do not publish raw identifiable review text or Steam user IDs.

```{r}

library(httr2)

get_game <- function(id) {
  # Wrap in tryCatch to handle missing/invalid IDs gracefully
  tryCatch({
    res <- request("https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails") |> 
      req_url_query(appids = id, cc = "us", l = "english") |> 
      req_retry(max_tries = 3, backoff = ~ 2) |> # Automatically handles rate limits (429s)
      req_perform()
    
    resp_body_json(res, simplifyVector = FALSE)
  }, error = function(e) {
    message(paste("Error fetching ID:", id, "-", e$message))
    return(NULL)
  })
}

# Loop with a built-in delay
for (i in 1:100) {
  print(paste("Fetching game:", i))
  game_data <- get_game(i)
  print(game_data)
  
  # Pause for 1.5 seconds between requests to respect Steam's servers
  Sys.sleep(1.5) 
}
Use code with caution.

🛠️ Key Improvements Made:

• Added Sys.sleep(1.5): Pauses the loop for 1.5 seconds after each request to stay well under Steam's rate limit


```

- I have access and a sample of the steam games and have looked into the data
to extract reviews, playtime, steamID #, name, release date, genre, price, etc.

- still want to look into steamCharts next for historical monthly player data


- at the moment I'm trying to figure out what games we should use
- i assumed it makes more sense, as to reduce randomness / variation, that we
could use games released in 2020 and compare their general longevity. So we can
look at games that flopped and games that lasted, all starting from 2020 where 
streaming / general longevity conditons where all on an equal field. For example, 
twitch wasn't around in 2010, so steam games from back then often wouldn't last as long,
or they wouldn't be as often in and out of main stream as they are now. 








```{r}

library(httr2)

get_game_name_2020 <- function(id) {
  tryCatch({
    res <- request("https://store.steampowered.com/api/appdetails") |> 
      req_url_query(appids = id, cc = "us", l = "english") |> 
      req_retry(max_tries = 3, backoff = ~ 2) |> 
      req_perform()
    
    body <- resp_body_json(res, simplifyVector = FALSE)
    id_str <- as.character(id)
    
    # Check if the API successfully returned data for this AppID
    if (!is.null(body[[id_str]]) && body[[id_str]]$success == TRUE) {
      game_data <- body[[id_str]]$data
      
      # Extract name and release date text
      game_name    <- game_data$name
      release_date <- game_data$release_date$date
      
      # Filter for dates containing the year "2020"
      if (!is.null(release_date) && grepl("2020", release_date)) {
        return(game_name)
      }
    }
    return(NULL)
  }, error = function(e) {
    return(NULL)
  })
}

# Vector to store our matching game names
games_2020 <- c()

# Loop through the first 100 AppIDs
for (i in 1:100) {
  name <- get_game_name_2020(i)
  
  if (!is.null(name)) {
    print(paste("Found 2020 game:", name))
    games_2020 <- c(games_2020, name)
  }
  
  Sys.sleep(1.5) # Maintain a safe rate limit to avoid 429 errors
}

# Print final filtered list
print("--- 2020 Games Found ---")
print(games_2020)




```
